name: Strict-Transport-Security
explanation: HSTS tells browsers to only connect over HTTPS for a set period, protecting users from protocol-downgrade and cookie-hijacking attacks.
recommendation: Set Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains on every HTTPS response.

name: Content-Security-Policy
explanation: CSP restricts which resources a page may load, sharply reducing the impact of cross-site scripting (XSS) and injection attacks.
recommendation: Add a Content-Security-Policy header with explicit source allowlists (start with default-src 'self' and tighten over time).

name: X-Frame-Options
explanation: Without clickjacking protection an attacker can embed the page in a transparent iframe and trick users into unintended actions.
recommendation: Set X-Frame-Options: DENY (or SAMEORIGIN if framing by same-origin pages is required).

name: X-Content-Type-Options
explanation: Without nosniff, browsers may guess the MIME type of a response, which can turn an upload into an executable script.
recommendation: Set X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff on all responses.

name: Referrer-Policy
explanation: Referrer-Policy controls how much of the previous URL is leaked to other sites, protecting sensitive query strings and paths.
recommendation: Set Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin (or no-referrer for highly sensitive applications).

name: Permissions-Policy
explanation: Permissions-Policy restricts which browser features (camera, microphone, geolocation) a page and its frames may use.
recommendation: Set Permissions-Policy with a restrictive default, e.g. Permissions-Policy: camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=().

name: Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy
explanation: CORP stops other origins from loading this site's resources, reducing cross-origin data leakage.
recommendation: Set Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy: same-origin unless cross-origin embedding is explicitly required.

name: X-Powered-By
explanation: The X-Powered-By header reveals the framework and often its version, giving attackers a head start on known vulnerabilities.
recommendation: Remove the X-Powered-By header (or disable the framework option that adds it).

name: X-XSS-Protection
explanation: X-XSS-Protection is deprecated: modern browsers ignore it, and in some configurations it can introduce vulnerabilities. Content-Security-Policy is the replacement.
recommendation: Remove the X-XSS-Protection header and rely on Content-Security-Policy instead.
